content: Yeah, thinks like morphic will remain slow for non allocation related reasons (though morphic also doesn't do arena allocation which maybe could help its perf a bit).
Is morphic just alias analysis?

I think morphic does analysis on uniqueness to enable inplace mutation without checking the refcount. It might also enable removing some refcount increments/decrements. That said, I don't think it currently works. I had to disable a chunk of its analysis due to causing bugs and it basically had no impact on perf for most benchmarks.
Cool, that would allow us to remove a dependency :smile:
Once Roc works consistently, we can re-enable it
But we are definitely not there right now
This is probably the biggest roc app I know of https://github.com/lukewilliamboswell/roc-htmx-tailwindcss-demo
I had one more advanced that this I was messing around with for a work project/prototype... I should probably back-port features from that into this demo.

I think it would be great to double check with someone who understands what it is supposed to do better before just removing it.

To be fair, it may be the case they we aren't leaning on it enough. Potentially more zig biultins could be using it's inplace vs not indicator at comptime. On top of that, it may not show huge gains until hit in a hot loop where removing the refcounting completely could be huge....but I don't know enough about it to be sure.

From what I know of it currently, it is bugged, it really slows down compile time (all the worst compile times I have ever seen have been due to morphic), and it doesn't generally affect perf much.

So that does push towards removing it assuming we can't easily fix it and make it algorithmically sound.

EDIT: all that said, not trying to be mean to the morphic folks. It might be a great piece of tech we are holding wrong or that has some minor bugs that happen to lead to scary roc issues.

import cli.Stdout
import cli.Utc exposing [now!, since]
import cli.Duration exposing [to_millis]

prime_bench : U64 -> I64
prime_bench = |start| {
  loopi = |cmps, i| {
      s0 = (i + i) * (i + 3) + 3
      if (s0 >= 131072) cmps else {
          elem = cmps.get(i.shr_zf_wrap(3)).ok_or(0.U8)
          msk = 1.U8.shl_wrap(i.bitwise_and(7).to_u8_wrap())
          if (elem.bitwise_and(msk) > 0) loopi(cmps, i + 1) else {
              bp = i + i + 3
              slmt = s0 + bp.shl_wrap(3)
              loops = |s, cs| {
                  if (s >= slmt) cs else {
                      smsk = 1.U8.shl_wrap(s.bitwise_and(7).to_u8_wrap())
                      updtf = |a| { a.bitwise_or(smsk) }
                      cull = |c, cp| {
                          if (c >= 16384) cp else {
                              cull(c + bp, List.update(cp, c, updtf).ok_or(cp))
                          }
                      }
                      loops(s + bp, cull(s.shr_zf_wrap(3), cs))
                  }
              }
              loopi(loops(s0, cmps), i + 1)
          }
      }
  }
  cmpsts = (1..=100).iter().fold(List.repeat(0.U8, 16384), |buf, _| loopi(buf, 0.U64 + start))
  cmpsts.fold(131073.I64, |cnt, e| cnt - e.count_one_bits().to_i64())
}

main! = |args| {
    # an external input so that compiler doesn't optimize away the repetition;
    # this defaults to zero when no argument is passed, which is fine...
    seed = match List.get(args, 1) {
        Ok(arg_os_str) =>
            arg_os_str.display() |> U64.from_str() |> Try.ok_or(0.U64)
        Err(_) => 0
    }    start = now!()
    answr = prime_bench(seed)
    stop = now!()
    elpsd = stop.since(start).to_millis()

    Stdout.line!("Found ${answr.to_str()} primes to 262146 in ${elpsd.to_str()} milliseconds.")
}```

The main problem is retaining cp as the error default across its update, which prevents efficient buffer reuse. The refactor consumes the list, uses direct loops and get/set, and measures with a monotonic clock.

Takes 7ms

Here is a faster version GPT Sol 6.1 edited for me 

# Build with Roc nightly-2026-11-13-03dce41 or later:
#   roc build examples/prime-bench.roc
# Run: ./examples/prime-bench [seed=0] [repeats=100]
app [main!] {
    cli: platform "https://github.com/roc-lang/basic-cli/releases/download/0.28.1/7brgwR8YUqfeGrkdfF1V4GPPN7DnP7ftqub9KcrTEZtr.tar.zst",
}

import cli.Stdout
import cli.Monotonic
import cli.Duration

prime_bench : U64, U64 -> I64
prime_bench = |seed, repeats| {
    # Bit i represents the odd number 2*i + 3; prime 2 is counted separately.
    var $composites = List.repeat(0.U8, 16384)
    var $repeat = 0.U64
    while $repeat < repeats {
        var $i = seed
        # i = 254 is the last index whose prime square fits in the bitmap.
        while $i < 255 {
            elem = match $composites.get($i.shr_zf_wrap(3)) {
                Ok(byte) => byte
                Err(_) => crash "Sieve candidate index out of bounds"
            }
            mask = (1.U8).shl_wrap($i.bitwise_and(7).to_u8_wrap())
            if elem.bitwise_and(mask) == 0 {
                prime = $i + $i + 3
                square_index = ($i + $i) * ($i + 3) + 3
                limit = square_index + prime.shl_wrap(3)
                var $s = square_index
                # Eight streams: each visits one fixed bit in successive bytes.
                while $s < limit {
                    stream_mask = (1.U8).shl_wrap($s.bitwise_and(7).to_u8_wrap())
                    var $byte_index = $s.shr_zf_wrap(3)
                    while $byte_index < 16384 {
                        old_byte = match $composites.get($byte_index) {
                            Ok(value) => value
                            Err(_) => crash "Sieve stream index out of bounds"
                        }
                        # Consume the old list; retaining it as an error default
                        # would require preserving its contents across the update.
                        $composites = match $composites.set($byte_index, old_byte.bitwise_or(stream_mask)) {
                            Ok(updated) => updated
                            Err(_) => crash "Sieve stream index out of bounds"
                        }
                        $byte_index = $byte_index + prime
                    }
                    $s = $s + prime
                }
            }
            $i = $i + 1
        }
        # Preserve the original benchmark: repeat culling the same bitmap.
        $repeat = $repeat + 1
    }
    var $count = 131073.I64
    var $index = 0.U64
    while $index < 16384 {
        byte = match $composites.get($index) {
            Ok(value) => value
            Err(_) => crash "Sieve count index out of bounds"
        }
        $count = $count - byte.count_one_bits().to_i64()
        $index = $index + 1
    }
    $count
}

main! = |args| {
    # Nonzero seeds skip sieve candidates; use zero to count all primes.
    seed = match args.get(0) {
        Ok(arg) => U64.from_str(arg.display()).ok_or(0)
        Err(_) => 0
    }
    repeats = match args.get(1) {
        Ok(arg) => U64.from_str(arg.display()).ok_or(100)
        Err(_) => 100
    }
    start = Monotonic.now!()
    answer = prime_bench(seed, repeats)
    elapsed = Monotonic.now!().since(start).to_millis()
    Stdout.line!("Found ${answer.to_str()} primes to 262146 in ${elapsed.to_str()} milliseconds (${repeats.to_str()} repeats).")
}

app [main!] {
    cli: platform "https://github.com/roc-lang/basic-cli/releases/download/0.28.0/2yhxoR7cZPSYbyUzPWULFw8AA6QEcdsgFNRmzu7pZbst.tar.zst",

import cli.Stdout
import cli.Utc exposing [now!, since]
import cli.Duration exposing [to_millis]

cull_pass : List(U8), U64, U64, U8 -> List(U8)
cull_pass = |cs, c0, bp, smsk| {
    limit = List.len(cs)
    var $c = c0
    var $cp = cs
    while $c < limit {
        $cp = match List.get($cp, $c) {
            Ok(old) => match List.set($cp, $c, old.bitwise_or(smsk)) {
                Ok(l) => l
                Err(_) => $cp
            }
            Err(_) => $cp
        }
        $c = $c.plus_wrap(bp)
    }
    $cp
}

prime_bench : U64 -> I64
prime_bench = |start| {
  loopi = |cmps, i| {
      s0 = (i + i) * (i + 3) + 3
      if (s0 >= 131072) cmps else {
          elem = cmps.get(i.shr_zf_wrap(3)).ok_or(0.U8)
          msk = 1.U8.shl_wrap(i.bitwise_and(7).to_u8_wrap())
          if (elem.bitwise_and(msk) > 0) loopi(cmps, i + 1) else {
              bp = i + i + 3
              slmt = s0 + bp.shl_wrap(3)
              loops = |s, cs| {
                  if (s >= slmt) cs else {
                      smsk = 1.U8.shl_wrap(s.bitwise_and(7).to_u8_wrap())
                      loops(s + bp, cull_pass(cs, s.shr_zf_wrap(3), bp, smsk))
                  }
              }
              loopi(loops(s0, cmps), i + 1)
          }
      }
  }
  cmpsts = (1..=100).iter().fold(List.repeat(0.U8, 16384), |buf, _| loopi(buf, 0.U64 + start))
  cmpsts.fold(131073.I64, |cnt, e| cnt - e.count_one_bits().to_i64())
}

main! = |args| {
    # an external input so that compiler doesn't optimize away the repetition;
    # this defaults to zero when no argument is passed, which is fine...
    seed = match List.get(args, 1) {
        Ok(arg_os_str) =>
            arg_os_str.display() |> U64.from_str() |> Try.ok_or(0.U64)
        Err(_) => 0
    }    start = now!()
    answr = prime_bench(seed)
    stop = now!()
    elpsd = stop.since(start).to_millis()

    Stdout.line!("Found ${answr.to_str()} primes to 262146 in ${elpsd.to_str()} milliseconds.")

Richard Feldman said:

I'm not sure what the C version you're comparing against is, but here's the roc code that I'm seeing get 1.6% more instructions at --opt=speed

Here is the C code I am using as a reference:

#include <stdio.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int primesBench() {
    unsigned char *cmpsts = malloc(16384);
    for (int i = 0; i < 16384; ++i) cmpsts[i] = 0;
    for (int n = 1; n <= 100000; ++n) {
        for (int i = 0; ; ++i) {
            int s0 = (i + i) * (i + 3) + 3;
            if (s0 >= 131072) break;
            if (cmpsts[i >> 3] & (1 << (i & 7))) continue;
            int bp = i + i + 3;
            int slmt = s0 + 8 * bp;
            for (int s = s0; s < slmt; s += bp) {
                unsigned char msk = 1 << (s & 7);
                for (int c = s >> 3; c < 16384; c += bp) cmpsts[c] |= msk;
            }
        }
    }
    int cnt = 131073;
    for (int i = 0; i < 131072; ++i) cnt -= cmpsts[i >> 3] >> (i & 7) & 1;
    free(cmpsts);
    return cnt;
}

int main() {
    clock_t start = clock();
    int answr = primesBench();
    double elpsd = (double)(clock() - start) / CLOCKS_PER_SEC * 1000;
    printf("Found %d primes up to 262146 in %f milliseconds.\r\n", answr, elpsd);
    return 0;
}
